cases.title: Antimagic suppresses local new cast, not remote buff
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-01-A: A caster inside the active sphere commits an otherwise legal rank-five spell, spending10RP and its ordinary cadence. Its payload is suppressed and receives no later delayed resolution on leaving. An already-established remote buff outside the sphere is not canceled merely because its concentrating caster entered it.
cases.currentInitialState: Wizard9 inside operative Lesser Antimagic; RP32; rank5 spell legal; separate ally outside carries an already-established remote buff whose manifestation never intersects field.
actionsAndResolution: Wizard commits the rank5 spell: Action/components and 10 RP are paid; ordinary cadence/concentration transition occurs.
Because the new spell payload originates inside operative Lesser Antimagic, its magical payload is suppressed at resolution with no queued later effect.
The remote buff outside remains active because only its caster—not its manifestation—entered the field.
cases.currentAdjudication: New cast costs remain spent and produces no delayed payload; remote outside buff persists to its own deadline.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Antimagic buffer/item/history
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-01-B: A body-attached magical buffer has12remaining when the bearer enters. It cannot absorb a new8damage packet inside; leaving within its original lifetime restores the same12remaining, not20and not an8HP refund. Ordinary stone already created by an instantaneous material spell remains real, and two Lesser Antimagic fields do not switch each other on and off indefinitely.
cases.currentInitialState: Creature enters field with an ongoing magical buffer showing 12 remaining; also carries ordinary stone already created by a completed instantaneous material spell. Two Lesser Antimagic fields overlap.
actionsAndResolution: While bearer intersects field, buffer is unavailable and cannot absorb an 8-damage packet; its remaining balance stays 12 and original expiry continues.
Stone remains ordinary matter because completed material creation is not rewound.
Same-family Lesser Antimagic fields are exempt from suppressing each other and create one union of active volume.
Leaving before buffer expiry restores access to same remaining 12; no HP refund.
cases.currentAdjudication: No queued prevention, no stone deletion, no field oscillation.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Greater Dispel shared higher-rank check
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-03-A: The snapshot includes a rank2buff, rank5field and two recipient records from one rank6cast. The first two end automatically. Wizard+8rolls15for23against rank6DC22, so both captured rank6recipient applications end using that one success. An unselected remote recipient remains unless the original source truly binds it to the ended parent.
cases.currentInitialState: Wizard9 Greater Dispel caster: INT+4 PB4 -> +8. Snapshot captures one rank2 buff, one rank5 field and two recipient applications from one rank6 generating cast.
actionsAndResolution: Rank2 and rank5 applications end automatically.
For original rank6 generating cast, roll once: d20=15 +8 =23 vs DC22 (10+2×6): success.
Reuse that one success for both captured rank6 recipient applications.
cases.currentAdjudication: Both captured rank6 applications end. Any remote application from same cast outside snapshot remains unless parent source says otherwise.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Snapshot does not expand
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-03-B: An eligible wall blocks another effect when the purge snapshot is taken. Ending that wall does not add the formerly hidden effect to this cast. A rank6check rolling natural20+0against22 uses the reviewed natural improvement from Failure to Success; no standard-game flat natural20 rule or free protected-effect identification is substituted.
cases.currentInitialState: Greater Dispel snapshot: rank5 Wall of Force portion is in sphere and blocks center LoE to another effect at capture time. Separate rank6 check fixture has +0 and d20=20 vs DC22.
actionsAndResolution: Capture snapshot before endings; hidden effect behind wall is excluded.
Rank5 wall ends automatically; snapshot remains frozen and hidden effect is not added.
For rank6 fixture, total20 vs DC22 is ordinary Failure; current natural-shift rule improves the degree once to Success, so captured rank6 effect ends.
cases.currentAdjudication: No second scan, no protected-effect identification, no generic 'natural20 always succeeds' replacement.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Spell Resistance direct and ending saves
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-04-A: A recipient makes the original WIS save against a hostile spell and later that spell's printed WIS ending save. Both gain ordinary advantage while this hour-long ward operates. If a separate source imposes disadvantage, normal cancellation yields one ordinary roll, not multiple advantage dice or a reroll after seeing failure.
cases.currentInitialState: Protected target has one hostile spell requiring initial WIS save and a later printed WIS ending save; another source imposes disadvantage.
actionsAndResolution: Initial save is directly required by spell: Spell Resistance supplies advantage; opposing disadvantage cancels to one normal roll.
Later printed ending save is still dependent on same spell: same rule.
No extra reroll after seeing result.
cases.currentAdjudication: Exactly ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation; no multi-advantage dice.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Spell attack vs downstream concentration
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-04-B: A spell attack damages the warded creature. The attack receives no automatic disadvantage, and the creature's resulting generic concentration save does not gain Spell Resistance merely because the damage came from a spell. A charge-based item actually casting a save-requiring spell does qualify, regardless of whether it charged the caster RP.
cases.currentInitialState: Protected creature is hit by a spell attack and separately must make an ordinary concentration save from damage. Separate source-recognized charge/use-only spell fixture forces a save.
actionsAndResolution: Spell attack roll receives no disadvantage from Spell Resistance.
Generic concentration save is caused by damage/life rule, not directly by a spell save instruction: no Spell Resistance advantage.
A genuine charge/use-only activation that is actually a spell and directly forces a save does receive the ward's advantage regardless of RP pricing.
cases.currentAdjudication: Provenance controls; pricing does not classify a technique as a spell.
notes: The historical example does not itself identify a named ancestry token; this current adjudication preserves only the source-recognized charge/use-only spell category. AC5-X06 handles the price-interface comparison separately.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Force wall physical and LoE barrier
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-05-A: An invisible vertical wall blocks an arrow and a directly targeted spell whose path must cross it, though a viewer can see the opponent through ordinary light. The caster cannot bypass the effect barrier simply by choosing a damage-area center beyond it. A real open route around its finite edge remains available.
cases.currentInitialState: Invisible vertical Wall of Force lies between archer/caster and visible enemy; finite edge has an open route around it.
actionsAndResolution: Arrow intersects wall and cannot pass.
Directly targeted spell requiring ordinary LoE through wall is illegal/blocked despite visual sight.
Caster cannot place a new ordinary area origin beyond wall without required originating LoE.
A creature may move around the real finite edge by ordinary movement.
cases.currentAdjudication: Light/vision through wall does not grant physical/spell path through it.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Force-wall support and safe resumption
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-05-B: A legal horizontal wall supports a creature until concentration ends, then actual Falling starts at that height. If a portion is suppressed and a body straddles it when suppression ends, local restoration waits for legal clearance; it neither bisects the body nor grants a free push to a tactically chosen square.
cases.currentInitialState: Horizontal Wall of Force supports creature at height. Later one wall segment is suppressed while a body occupies the closing segment.
actionsAndResolution: While active, horizontal wall provides support.
When concentration ends, all support ends and ordinary Falling starts from current height.
For separate suppression fixture, suppressed portion is absent; on resumption occupied portion remains locally pending until body clears; no bisect/shove.
cases.currentAdjudication: No free displacement or support after source ending.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

Later 17 post-defense eligible damage: pool prevents17, leaving43 and residual0.

A received transferred branch explicitly bypassing prevention leaves the pool unchanged. A new40point offer against43remaining loses the strongest-only comparison and does not refresh that old source, despite the new actual payment.

actionsAndResolution: Price=base10 + Dissonance1 + protectedX2 =13. creditable base10; pool offer60, not65.
Transferred branch explicitly marked unmitigated arrives after original prevention stage and cannot consume Barrier.
Separate weaker/equal offer40 against existing43 is paid but does not refresh retained source/expiry.

cases.title: Reputation signed contributions
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-08-A: In one actual scene the protected character receives a legitimate+1contribution and a−2contribution. The latter is recorded as prevented0; the net unprevented+1uses the ordinary scene/absolute caps. The shield does not force NPCs to forgive the underlying act or erase evidence, and no−2debt appears after24hours.
cases.currentInitialState: Protected character standing0 receives one +1 and one -2 institutional contribution in same scene under current signed-ledger rules.
actionsAndResolution: Record +1 normally.
Record -2 event/provenance, replace contribution with0 while shield operative.
Apply ordinary scene/absolute caps to unprevented net +1.
cases.currentAdjudication: Standing becomes+1. Underlying act/evidence/NPC reactions remain; no -2 debt after expiry.

cases.title: Reputation rise, standing cost and suppression
cases.historicalOriginalText: AB5-08-B: The character gains standing from+1to+2while protected; later genuine negative contributions are still blocked rather than merely allowing a fall back to the original+1. A voluntary transaction requiring payment of1standing cannot obtain its benefit for free. During a genuine suppression interval, a new ordinary penalty may lower standing and is not rolled back when protection resumes.
cases.currentInitialState: Character starts standing+1, rises to+2 while protected. Later a real -1 consequence, then a voluntary transaction requiring 1 standing, then a suppression interval with new -1 event.
actionsAndResolution: Protected -1 is recorded/prevented0; standing stays+2.
Standing-cost transaction cannot proceed free while shield prevents negative payment; target may end shield first to pay.
During actual suppression, new -1 applies normally. Resumption does not restore it.
cases.currentAdjudication: Shield is prospective negative-contribution prevention, not floor/escrow/social control.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

A perceived foe still adjacent at its next regular START fails the aura DEX and takes1d6=5fire. These are the one commanded attack plus the explicitly printed passive aura, not permission for a second companion Action.

actionsAndResolution: Owner spends one legal Bonus Action command; attached pet attack hits and rolls2d10=12 fire. Attack root dealer=pet.
At target's next regular START, aura eligibility passes; DEX save fails; shared aura d6=5; recipient aura root dealer=pet; take5 before defenses.

cases.title: Fire Pet aura frequency

Entry itself deals nothing; only its actual future regular START can attempt the family tick, with one owner/target history for the round. Replacing the pet or granting the foe an extra turn cannot reset that history or turn the pet into free fuel.
cases.currentInitialState: One foe moves across/into/out of aura three times during one turn; later receives an extra turn in same numbered round. Owner perceives hostility.
actionsAndResolution: Entry/crossing never triggers aura.
At first future regular START within5ft, one aura attempt may occur.
Family history prevents another aura attempt for same owner/target/Greater-Fire-Pet family in same numbered round even after replacement or extra turn.

cases.title: Blast range vs radius and hostile information

All perceived qualifying enemies with center line of effect are included, while an unseen presumed enemy is not revealed or selected from hidden allegiance data. There is no finite target-count cap to redistribute after a save.

actionsAndResolution: Center is legal because casting-point range is20ft.
Every perceived qualifying hostile inside radius+center LoE is included; no numerical cap.
Unseen/suspected enemy is not automatically identified/selected.

t6 child packet6 fire; t12 child3; t18 child9.
After third opportunity rider ends.

cases.title: Living Magma suppression consumes ordinal
cases.historicalOriginalText: CJ5-03-B: The second START occurs while the rider is suppressed and is consumed without a roll/damage. The third remains its original last opportunity. A bucket of water does not remove this non-Burning spell record, and a later successful initial CON save against another cast does not erase the existing application.
cases.currentInitialState: Target failed initial save; second scheduled START is under actual suppression; third is not. Separate new cast later succeeds on initial CON.
actionsAndResolution: First tick resolves normally.
Second scheduled opportunity is suppressed: consume ordinal; no roll, packet or child root.
Third remains final opportunity.
Later successful new-cast save does not replace/end existing older rider because new rider never establishes.

Its Nexus price is8in either case; subsequent reviewed Ease can make that7. The actual rank remains5and its normal Dissonance gain remains; no2RP is also recovered into the pool.

cases.title: Nexus replacement and Ready timing
cases.historicalOriginalText: CJ5-06-B: A Wizard replacing their own concentration Nexus ends the old concentration at commitment, so cannot rely on that disappearing field to price the new cast at8. A genuinely separate other-owner field still present can qualify. A readied cast paid inside keeps that paid price when released outside, with no second discount or refund.
cases.currentInitialState: Wizard maintains own Nexus and wants to cast replacement; separate fixture has another owner's Nexus. Readied spell is committed inside field then released outside.
actionsAndResolution: Starting replacement concentration ends own old Nexus at commitment before new cast can use it; own old field gives no discount.
Another owner's already-operative Nexus may qualify.
Readied spell prices once at preparation/commitment; later release outside does not reprice/refund.
cases.currentAdjudication: No self-financed concentration replacement; no release-time second discount.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Champion cap, standing drift and cargo
cases.historicalOriginalText: CJ5-07-B: The caster cannot create one champion from each of three friendly factions to gain three source slots; this spell permits one per owner across all factions. An actual later standing decrease does not duplicate or teleport a real officer into its body. On expiry a genuinely borrowed lantern drops intact, while the manifested weapon leaves no harvestable item or NPC corpse.
cases.currentInitialState: Caster has three friendly factions but only one live Champion. Existing Champion carries genuine borrowed lantern and intrinsic manifested weapon. Standing later drops.
actionsAndResolution: Spell permits one Champion per owner across all factions; second successful formation replaces first rather than adds another.
Later ordinary standing loss does not remotely end already admitted body.
At source expiry body ends; real lantern drops/settles at last legal position; intrinsic weapon vanishes.
cases.currentAdjudication: No teleported officer, corpse/loot, faction stock duplication or source-slot multiplication.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Nexus + Dampening + Ease and base-only waiver
cases.currentInitialState: Fixture A: Wizard9 casts rank5 base10 spell while body intersects one Nexus and one accepted Dampening Field, with pending Ease. Fixture B: Wizard20 uses Grand Reservoir /cards/62 for same legal rank5 spell inside both fields with pending Ease.
actionsAndResolution: A: ordinary base10 -> Nexus8 -> Dampening mandatory+2=10 -> Ease -1=9. Pay9 RP; spell remains rank5.

B: Grand Reservoir waives normal/base RP cost to0 but not mandatory extras. Nexus has no remaining ordinary RP-price component to reduce ->0. Dampening creates mandatory +2 interface ->2. Ease ->1. Spend Grand Reservoir use and pay1 RP if Wizard has a pool; components/cadence remain.
cases.currentAdjudication: Accepted Dampening ordering is unchanged; Nexus never moves after it and never discounts protected/created Dampening extra.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Charge/use-only spell versus RP-paid nonspell
cases.currentInitialState: Fixture A uses a legitimately pre-existing charge/use-only ancestry casting entitlement for actual Burning Hands; this review does not create that ancestry grant. Caster has an RP pool and stands inside Nexus+Dampening. Fixture B is Ranger Nature's Whisper /cards/7 with RP5 inside both fields.
actionsAndResolution: A: Burning Hands remains an actual spell. Its ancestry route has no ordinary RP-price interface, so Nexus has 0 discountable RP and does nothing. Accepted Dampening adds its scoped +2 RP interface; the ancestry charge/use is still spent. If the caster had no RP pool, the cast would be unaffordable. Burning Hands keeps its own Action/components/save/damage.

B: Nature's Whisper is magical NONSPELL, Action1RP, Recharge3, spellRank null. Nexus and Dampening do not alter its1RP cost. It commits1RP and Recharge3 under its own card; Lesser Antimagic can suppress its magical payload only by the field's explicit nonspell scope.
cases.currentAdjudication: RP payment does not classify a technique as a spell; Nexus does not manufacture an RP price for charge/use-only spells.
notes: The packet recognizes charge-only ancestry spell routes but does not include a specific ancestry-grant card. The fixture therefore presumes an already legitimate campaign entitlement; it does not author one.
cases.evidenceKind: authored adjudication example; not runtime/human/balance test

cases.title: Antimagic vs Dimensional Door endpoints
cases.currentInitialState: Fixture A: Wizard outside Lesser Antimagic at origin O; known legal same-plane Dimensional Door destination D also outside; a drawn straight line O-D crosses the sphere. Fixture B: same caster's body is actually inside the field at commitment.
actionsAndResolution: A: Dimensional Door has no traversed path/LoE requirement to known destination. Lesser Antimagic does not invent one, so crossing a drawn line is irrelevant; cast resolves if its own endpoint rules pass.

B: Wizard may legally commit Door if casting permissions/resources pass; costs/cadence are spent. Because spell manifestation originates in operative antimagic volume, payload is suppressed and body remains at O. No delayed teleport occurs on exit.
cases.currentAdjudication: Local suppression is not a universal beam/path engine.
